html:
The last and longest-lived Korean dynasty, which ruled from 1392 until Japan annexed Korea in 1910. It was founded by the general Yi Seong-gye, King Taejo, who overthrew Goryeo, and it moved the capital to Hanyang, modern Seoul.

Joseon made Neo-Confucianism, the school of Zhu Xi, its ruling creed. Family rites, education and law followed Confucian rules, and Buddhism lost its old place. Officials were chosen by exams on the classics, and a hereditary elite, the yangban, dominated them. Scholars such as Yi Hwang made Korea a centre of Confucian thought.

High points:

  • Sejong the Great had the Hangul alphabet created in 1443, a simple script for writing Korean.
  • Royal workshops built rain gauges and water clocks.
  • The palace of Gyeongbokgung and the fortress of Hwaseong.

Disasters followed in the 1590s and 1600s. Japan invaded in the Imjin War of 1592 to 1598; the admiral Yi Sun-sin beat its fleets but the land was wrecked. Manchu invasions in 1627 and 1636 made Joseon a vassal of the Qing. Joseon then closed itself to most foreign contact and was called the hermit kingdom in the West. It still had two centuries of peace and growth.

In the 19th century Japan forced it open with the Treaty of Ganghwa in 1876. Reforms and rebellions followed. Joseon renamed itself the Korean Empire in 1897, but Japan made it a protectorate in 1905 and annexed it in 1910.
